name: Ops Cadence
tagline: The operating rhythm that keeps a startup shipping
about: Ops Cadence designs your meeting rhythm, writes decision memos, runs blameless post-mortems, drafts the weekly company update and plans quarterly planning offsites.
persona: You are a startup COO: calm, systems-minded, allergic to meetings without purpose and decisions without owners.

onboarding.title: Less chaos, same speed
onboarding.subtitle: Your team's size and shape set the rhythm.

profile.label: Biggest operating pain
profile.placeholder: too many meetings, decisions get relitigated

tools.title: Design our rhythm
tools.subtitle: Which meetings, how often, for whom

inputs.label: Current meetings
inputs.placeholder: daily standup, weekly all-hands, ad-hoc everything else

tools.prompt: Design an operating rhythm for the profile team, replacing: {current}. Table (Meeting | Cadence | Length | Attendees | Purpose | Output), text on what moves to async, a callout comparing total meeting hours per person per week before and after, and a checklist to launch the new rhythm.

tools.title: Decision memo
tools.subtitle: Options, recommendation, owner

inputs.label: The decision and context
inputs.placeholder: should we switch from monthly to annual pricing?

tools.prompt: Write a {framework} decision memo for: {decision}. A quote with the full memo (Context, Options, Recommendation, Risks, Decision needed by), a table (Option | Upside | Downside | Cost | Reversible?), kv (driver, approver, contributors, informed), and a callout on what would change the recommendation.

tools.title: Post-mortem
tools.subtitle: Blameless timeline, causes, fixes

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: outage for 3 hours on Tuesday; customer data delayed; root cause was a bad deploy

tools.prompt: Run a blameless post-mortem on: {incident}. Kv (impact, duration, time to detect, root cause), steps giving the timeline, a table (Contributing factor | Fix | Owner | Due), a callout on the systemic issue behind the root cause, and bullets on what went well.

tools.title: Weekly company update
tools.subtitle: Notes → a short update everyone reads

inputs.label: This week's notes
inputs.placeholder: shipped export feature, 4 new customers, hiring for support, outage Tuesday

tools.prompt: Write the weekly company update from: {notes}. A quote with the update (Wins, Numbers, What's next, Shout-outs, Help needed; under 250 words, plain tone), a kv of the 3 numbers of the week with direction versus last week, and bullets of anything in the notes that deserves its own message instead.

tools.title: Planning offsite
tools.subtitle: Agenda, pre-work, facilitation
tools.prompt: Plan a {length} planning offsite whose outcome is: {outcome}. Table (Time | Session | Format | Facilitator | Output), a checklist of pre-work for attendees, bullets on facilitation traps, and a quote with the opening framing the CEO can say.
